intro_en: This segment of the Israel National Trail combines urban walking, antiquities sites and a beautiful forest of Mount Tabor oaks, notable for its wonderful winter bloom.
character_en: (For those walking from the north) This segment has 3 distinct parts: the eastern part is urban and runs alongside roads in Nazareth and Mashhad; the middle part combines nature with antiquities and heritage sites; the western part crosses a beautiful Mount Tabor oak forest, lovely all year round and especially in late winter and early spring. Most of the walk is a gentle descent on comfortable paths. There is one short climb of moderate difficulty up to Mitzpe Reish Lakish.
transport_en: Har Yona neighbourhood in Nof HaGalil (Nazareth Illit), HaMovil Interchange
pois_en: Remains of antiquities: the aqueduct to Tzippori, a large winepress and more. The tomb of Rabbi Yehuda Nesiah. The scenery of the Mount Tabor oak forest and its late-winter and early-spring bloom
important_en: The trail passes near the entrance to Tzippori National Park but does not enter it. Entry to the national park is subject to a fee.
At the tomb compound of Rabbi Yehuda Nesiah there is drinking water and there are picnic tables. The access road to it runs through Moshav Tzippori.

For a vehicle pick-up at the end of the route, it is best to finish at the Paz petrol station east of HaMovil Interchange, where it is safe to park. The trail itself passes about 300 metres south of the station and it is easy to leave the trail and reach it.
In the urban section, mainly in Mashhad, the markings may change if there are construction or road works.
description_en:
The route begins next to the cemetery near Har Yona, and skirts the Har Yona neighbourhood along Ma'ale Yitzhak Street in Nof HaGalil (Nazareth Illit). After the street curves left, the trail leaves the street to the right towards Mashhad, on a short descent along a dirt road.
Follow the markings through Mashhad and exit on the western side of the town. South of the grocery store is a small hill called Tel Gath-Hepher; some believe this is the site of biblical Gath-Hepher.
After a short walk on asphalt, the trail becomes a dirt road that crosses pine groves. The trail descends north-west, and continues west to a pine grove next to the entrance to Tzippori National Park. In the grove are the remains of a stone embankment that carried an aqueduct bringing water from Ein Mashhad to ancient Tzippori. (The most impressive part of the site is a huge underground water reservoir, located within the national park, which charges an entrance fee.)
From the junction of dirt roads east of the national park, the trail descends north, skirts the park to the north-west and continues west. The trail passes south of the community of Hoshaya and reaches the tomb of Rabbi Yehuda Nesiah. He was the grandson of the compiler of the Mishnah, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, an important and famous religious leader known simply as 'Rabbi'. In the tomb compound you will find a water tap and picnic tables.
After the picnic and a look at the tomb building, we continue north-west along a jeep track, which the trail leaves after about 1 km. We then start climbing west on a slightly steep path that passes through a planted grove to Mitzpe Reish Lakish. The lookout is named after an important rabbi from the period of the Amoraim.
From the lookout, the trail heads west through a relaxed and beautiful stretch of open forest of large Mount Tabor oaks. Among the trees, thousands of flowers bloom in winter and spring. The trail passes an ancient winepress (a large treading floor and a settling pit).
Before HaMovil Interchange the trail passes through olive groves, and then descends through woodland to an underpass beneath Road 77 (the road between Tiberias and Ramat Yishai). After a short walk, we also cross Road 79 (the road between the Krayot and Nazareth) through an underpass, beneath the bridge over which Nahal Yiftahel, a tributary of Nahal Tzippori, flows. From here, the trail climbs to the end point on the access road to the community of Alon HaGalil.
nearby_en: A stroll among the market and churches of Nazareth, with many culinary options near the market and around the city.
Tzippori National Park: it is worth setting aside at least two hours for a visit.

Alon HaGalil: at the western end of this pretty community west of HaMovil Junction is the 'Fresco' coffee roastery. It is a good place to have a drink or buy a bag of coffee for the road and chat with Alon, the owner (it is advisable to arrange in advance, as it is sometimes closed). At the eastern end of the community, not far from the trail, is the visitor centre of the Ofir apiary.
Recommended lodging: Alon Tavor Field School
author_en: Omer Shapira, Content Coordinator, Tourism Division, Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel (SPNI).
